The Weeks Before a Wedding

For the weeks before a wedding, when the list grows faster than the time. It narrows down to the three things that matter, gets the budget said out loud, hands the questions to someone else, and plans for the drop that comes afterward.

Weddings · Stress · Family · Boundaries · 9 items · once a week

The checklist

  • Write down the three things that actually matter to you — the rest can go to whoever cares most about it.
  • Agree the budget number out loud with each other — a figure left unsaid becomes a fight later.
  • Give one person the job of handling questions — you should not be the switchboard for your own wedding.
  • Decide now who sits where and stop revisiting it — a seating plan expands to fill all available worry.
  • Keep one evening a week with no wedding talk — you are also still two people with a life.
  • Say no to one tradition you do not want — a day built on obligation is somebody else's day.
  • Write the hard conversation down before having it — who is not invited is better said once, clearly.
  • Put someone in charge of you eating on the day — people forget, and it shows by mid-afternoon.
  • Plan the week after as carefully as the day — the drop afterward catches almost everyone off guard.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it once a week, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
